observation_summary: The StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence) method fails to correctly compare two CharSequence objects because it relies on the default Object.equals() implementation, which is not guaranteed to be consistent across different CharSequence implementations.
reasoning_summary: The bug is in the procedural logic of the equals method. It incorrectly assumes that calling .equals() on two CharSequence objects will correctly determine if their character sequences are identical. Since the Java contract for CharSequence does not guarantee that .equals() compares the actual character content, the implementation needs to be updated to perform a character-by-character comparison (or equivalent) to correctly satisfy the intended functionality of StringUtils.equals(). This is a procedural/algorithmic correction rather than a missing guard or a design-level capability omission.
evidence_used: The bug report states that StringUtils.equals(CharSequence, CharSequence) relies on CharSequence#equals(Object), which is undefined for CharSequence implementations.

The failing test case shows that comparing a String with a StringBuilder or other CharSequence implementations fails, indicating the current implementation logic is insufficient for the intended purpose.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The capability (equality check) exists, but the implementation logic is flawed. It does not require a design-level change to the class structure, just a better implementation of the comparison algorithm.
The issue is not a mismatch in the interface contract between caller and callee, but rather an incorrect internal implementation of the comparison logic within the StringUtils class.
